newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, passed- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle bids early Tuesday at $64.00 per cwt were passed by owners asking $66.00 to $67.00, feedlot sources said.
"Buyers are showing a little more aggressive interest this morning than on Monday, but I'm not sure a bid at $65.00 would buy many cattle," one Kansas feedlot manager said.
Cattle owners were standing firm on their higher bids amid sentiment that packers will need to start buying cattle soon but from smaller showlists than a week ago, sources said.
Last week's active sales depleted showlists and kept feedlots extremely current, they said.
Fed cattle prices also were seen bolstered by continued support from beef prices, cattle feeders said.
"The higher beef on Monday and moderate movement should help them sit tough (on bids)," a feedlot manager said.

Beef cut-out prices on Monday were quoted up $0.61 to $0.74 per cwt, with 88 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $104.81, up $0.72 from Friday and up $2.06 since Wednesday's close when prices started trending higher, USDA statistics showed.
